No stairs/floors question at either address, despite re-quoting a job specifically to improve accuracy

top_strength: The trip-fee and No Worries explanations were the best moments of the call. On the $150 he did not just defend it — he explained the fifteen-mile free-travel radius, named Farmers Branch as the closest of four metroplex branches, and then closed the loop with 'that 150 that's built into that 1578 that I gave you, so there's no additional to that number,' which is exactly how you kill a hidden-fee worry. On insurance he ran the full contrast: the state-mandated 60 cents per pound per item that 'doesn't really account for anything,' then the $2,000 No Worries set aside per move to repair, replace or reimburse, then the two-to-three-business-day turnaround versus 'dragging you through a super long insurance claim.' He also did real customer-first work by cutting a three-mover, seven-hour quote down to two movers and saving the customer several hundred dollars.
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix: the Save Your Ass speech, and this call is the case study for why. Joe told you he has about fifty boxes and is moving a mile and a half down the road — that is a carload conversation begging to happen. The exact language: 'Joe, one thing I always tell people — everything you do before we get there is time you're not paying for. If you can get the loose stuff out of drawers, the pictures off the walls, the small boxes consolidated in one room, and take a carload or two over yourself since you're only a mile and a half away, that hour or two you save comes straight off the bill. Does that make sense?' That single block protects the estimate you just cut. Second priority: your estimate contradicted itself. You quoted five-to-seven hours at $1,578, then said a 1700 square foot house typically runs seven to eight hours with two movers — Joe now has two different numbers from the same call, and that is precisely how we end up outside the 20% accuracy window. Pick one range, state the hourly rate per mover so he can do the math himself, and name the variables that would move it (stairs, walk distance, box count). Third: you were eleven minutes into a re-quote before Joe had to ask your name. Open with 'This is Landon with Einstein Moving Company,' then the agenda — 'I'll gather some details, walk you through pricing, takes about ten to fifteen minutes, sound good?' — and use his name three or four times along the way. The Clock section was a clean zero: minimum, increments, and when the clock starts all need to be said out loud on every quote.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently courteous with steady 'yes sir' affirmations and a polite self-correction ('I had seen you — go ahead, I'm so sorry'), and the customer left the call positive, but the warmth stayed transactional: no name use until the final line, no empathy markers, and long rambling stretches with heavy self-correction rather than clean acknowledgment of what Joe said.
